name: Evergreen Protocol Definitions - v1.0
description: Version-pinned definitions for Evergreen Protocol v1.0. This file is stable and citable. Future versions must publish at new versioned paths.
governanceNote: This file is version-pinned to Evergreen Protocol v1.0. Do not overwrite it silently after publication; publish future versions at /protocol/v1.1/ or /protocol/v2/.
usageNotice: Static versioned reference. Not a certification, compliance verdict, live API endpoint, MCP endpoint, registry, or readiness checklist.

terms.definition: The governance discipline of maintaining the validity, version integrity, citeability, and operational coherence of institutional reference systems under accelerated change.
terms.boundaryNote: This is the governed category term. It does not claim to replace information security, data governance, AI model safety, content management, legal compliance, or risk management frameworks.

terms.definition: The gradual loss of validity, citeability, or operational coherence in a reference system through outdated content, undocumented changes, ambiguous ownership, or disconnection from the practices it governs.
terms.boundaryNote: Reference decay describes a governance risk in reference systems only. It is not a security incident, legal finding, or compliance verdict.

terms.definition: The challenge of maintaining reference validity in institutional environments where AI models, outputs, tools, teams, and regulatory conditions change faster than the governance structures that depend on them.
terms.boundaryNote: AI-era digital continuity frames accelerated reference change. It does not evaluate AI models, certify AI systems, or define AI safety controls.

terms.definition: A versioned, citable reference that defines the scope, vocabulary, and explicit boundaries of a specific governance category.
terms.boundaryNote: A category standard defines and documents a category. It does not certify, audit, impose legal obligations, or open a compliance registry.

terms.definition: A documented unit of governance with bounded scope, named roles, listed artifacts, acceptance criteria, and a defined review and versioning regime.
terms.boundaryNote: This term describes a governance pattern within the standard. It is not a product category, certification mark, or external recognition claim.

terms.definition: The structural layer: formal elements such as charter, roles, artifacts, acceptance criteria, and change control that give continuity a stable shape.
terms.boundaryNote: This layer structures reference governance only. It does not prescribe software architecture, security architecture, or implementation tooling.

terms.definition: The philosophical stance that unnecessary drift in definitions, exceptions, ownership, and surfaces is a manageable risk when made visible and reviewed.
terms.boundaryNote: This is a conceptual governance layer. It does not assert perfect control, literal permanence, or technical entropy measurement.

terms.definition: The operational commitment to tie reviews to validity and dependency change rather than fashion cycles or arbitrary urgency.
terms.boundaryNote: This term names review timing logic. It is not a mathematical algorithm, automated assessment, or scoring engine.

terms.definition: The explicit statement of what a protocol governs and what it does not govern.
terms.boundaryNote: A scope boundary clarifies coverage. It does not assign legal responsibility or certify that a system is inside or outside compliance.

terms.definition: An object used as evidence or as an operational interface to the protocol, including documents, registers, URLs, schemas, logs, or system screens.
terms.boundaryNote: An artifact supports reference traceability. Listing an artifact does not certify its quality, completeness, or compliance status.

terms.definition: A testable condition that distinguishes expected protocol operation from deviation.
terms.boundaryNote: Acceptance criteria are internal governance conditions. They are not public compliance tests, readiness scores, or certification checks.

terms.definition: The scheduled and event-triggered timetable for revisiting whether a protocol still matches reality, artifacts, and justified exceptions.
terms.boundaryNote: Review cadence defines when review occurs. It does not guarantee outcomes, approve organizations, or open a submission workflow.

terms.definition: A structured examination during review for drift modes such as tacit exceptions, definition forks, surface drift, and ownership vacuums.
terms.boundaryNote: An entropy check is a review activity. It is not an automated scanner, compliance audit, or live readiness checklist.

terms.definition: The practice of recording what changed in a reference system, when the change occurred, why it was made, and under whose authority.
terms.boundaryNote: Version discipline supports citation stability. It does not create a dynamic API, change registry, or external submission process.

terms.definition: The structural readiness to identify the governing reference, version, and responsible owner for protocols, decisions, and knowledge assets at the point of use.
terms.boundaryNote: Evidence posture is a reference governance concept. It is not an audit opinion, assurance report, or proof of external compliance.
